claims.text: A hosted service is a class the ASP.NET Core host starts when the app starts and stops when the app shuts down (IHostedService StartAsync/StopAsync), used for background work.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Background tasks with hosted services in ASP.NET Core (IHostedService interface)

claims.text: BackgroundService is a base class for a long-running IHostedService; subclasses override ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken), which the host runs once when the service starts.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Background tasks with hosted services, BackgroundService base class

claims.text: The CancellationToken passed to ExecuteAsync (stoppingToken) is triggered when IHostedService.StopAsync is called, i.e. when the app shuts down.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: BackgroundService ("The cancellation token is triggered when IHostedService.StopAsync is called")

claims.text: PeriodicTimer.WaitForNextTickAsync waits asynchronously for the next tick: no thread is blocked while it waits.
claims.source_hint: .NET API: System.Threading.PeriodicTimer, WaitForNextTickAsync

claims.text: IServiceScopeFactory is registered as a singleton by the DI container and CreateScope() returns a new IServiceScope whose ServiceProvider resolves scoped services; disposing the scope disposes them.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Dependency injection, service lifetimes / scope validation; IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope

claims.text: A hosted service runs in the same process as the app that serves requests; AddHostedService registers it with the app's host, not as a separate program.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Background tasks with hosted services; live: NotificationSender log lines in docker compose logs api

claims.text: NotificationSender's Tick is TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2): ExecuteAsync creates new PeriodicTimer(Tick) and loops while await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken), running one round per tick.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Api/Jobs/NotificationSender.cs:13, 25-39

claims.text: AddHostedService registers the hosted service as a singleton (IHostedService), so the host creates one instance for the life of the app.
claims.source_hint: .NET API: ServiceCollectionHostedServiceExtensions.AddHostedService (singleton IHostedService)

claims.text: DbContext is not thread-safe and is meant for one unit of work; AddDbContext registers DonHangDbContext as scoped, so it must not be held by a singleton for the app's life.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: DbContext lifetime, configuration, and initialization (default scoped; not thread-safe)

claims.text: Each round, SendDueAsync creates a scope with scopeFactory.CreateScope() (using var), resolves NotificationQueue and IEmailSender from it; NotificationQueue is scoped and takes DonHangDbContext; the scope is disposed when the method returns.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: NotificationSender.cs:47-59; DonHang.Infrastructure/NotificationQueue.cs:8; ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:17,25

claims.text: Since .NET 6, by default (BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost) an unhandled exception thrown from BackgroundService.ExecuteAsync is logged and the host stops.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Breaking change 6.0 'Unhandled exceptions from a BackgroundService'; HostOptions.BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior

claims.text: ExecuteAsync wraps each round in try/catch (Exception ex) when (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested), logging with LogError and continuing the loop; during shutdown the filter lets the exception out.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Api/Jobs/NotificationSender.cs:30-37

claims.text: When stoppingToken is cancelled, WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken) completes with OperationCanceledException; SendDueAsync gets the same token, so the calls that take it can stop early (by throwing OperationCanceledException), and the loop ends.
claims.source_hint: .NET API: PeriodicTimer.WaitForNextTickAsync (OperationCanceledException when token cancelled); NotificationSender.cs:28,32,53-58
